plan: In a second-price auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid), truthful bidding is the dominant strategy regardless of competitors' strategies. This holds true whether opponents are truthful, aggressive, or use any other strategy - bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit. My value is $27, so I will bid exactly $27. This ensures I only win when the prize is worth more to me than what I'll pay, and I capture full available surplus when I do win.

This is a second-price auction (winner pays the second-highest bid), which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win with a high second-highest bid; bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. With my value at $31, I should bid $31 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. With value $20, I should bid exactly $20 to maximize expected profit.
